** ** *
 JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-

That on 24-01-2024 at about 07-00 pm., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EL-6484 from Channarayapatna Housing Board to Srinivasapura and when he reached near N Bindenahalli cross road, Kasaba Hobli, C R Patna Taluk, at that time the rider by riding motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules, drove on the path hole of the road, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Channarayapatna Government Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to Grass Life Hospital, Channaryapatna, wherein admitted as an inpatient.

So far, the petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, nourishment food,
conveyance, and transportation etc.,
3.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 74 years.
He is agriculturalist and earning Rs.6,00,000/- per annum.
Due to the permanent disability, the petitioner is not in a position to do the said work as earlier and undergone tremendous pain, mental shock, agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In response to the notice, the respondent no.1 did not appear before this tribunal and remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

5. The respondent no.2 /the insurer of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EL-6484 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms Beeregowda C K vs Kumar on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182576943/
2 and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 contended that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident, that the petitioner, in collusion with the jurisdictional police and owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain and that there is delay of one day in lodging the complaint, that the rider of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license.
6. Heard the arguments on both sides.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 24-01-2024 at about 7-00 pm., when he was pillion rider in motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EL-6484 near N Bindenahalli cross road, Kasaba Hobli, C.R Patna Taluk, at that time rider of the said vehicle road the same in rash and negligent manner and drove the motorcycle into the path hole as a result he fell down and sustained severe injuries, as mentioned in the claim petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?
8. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and one witness is examined as PW.2 and marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
The respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

9. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative. Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle,
P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place, on 24-01-2024 at about 07-00 pm., when the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EL-6484 (hereinafter called the offending vehicle) from Channarayapatna Housing Board to Srinivasapura and when he reached near N Bindenahalli cross road, Kasaba Hobli, C R Patna Taluk

, at that time the rider by riding motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules, drove on the path hole of the road, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

The P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as F.I.R with Complaint, wound certificate, spot Beeregowda C K vs Kumar on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182576943/
3 mahazar, notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon, IMV report, Statement of witness,
charge sheet, etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Swamy C K, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.0036/2024 of Channarayapatna Town Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC r/w Sec.187 of MV Act.

13. The respondent no.2 in his written statement and during the cross examination of PW.1 has taken the contention that at the time of accident petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle and that since accident in question has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, if it is admitted that petitioner was riding the motorcycle, he will not get the compensation hence in order to get the compensation, the petitioner was falsely shown as pillion rider in the motorcycle.

14. So far as the aforesaid contention taken by the respondent no.2 is concerned, if the MLC and police intimation which is in the case sheet is perused, wherein it is clearly stated that the petitioner traveling in the two wheeler as pillion rider was met with an accident.
Further if the police documents are perused, one Dhananjaya was the RC owner of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, on the date of accident Dhananjaya was riding the motorcycle and petitioner was traveling in the said motorcycle as pillion rider.
When as per the records Dhananjaya was the RC owner of the offending vehicle, there is no reason to believe that petitioner was riding the motorcycle of Dhananjaya.
Hence, it can be said that petitioner was in the offending vehicle as pillion rider.
Admittedly, no other vehicle was involved in the accident.
When petitioner was riding the motorcycle as pillion rider, there is no possibility of petitioner contributing any amount of negligence in causing for the accident.
If the rider of the motorcycle ride the motorcycle in slow and steady manner by observing the path holes in the road, he could have avoided the accident.
Hence, it can be said that rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P2 and P8.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 24-01- 2024 to 31-01-2024 at Grass Life Hospital, Bengaluru, for a period of 8 days.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained three injuries of which injury no.1 is grievous in nature and injury no.2 and 3 are simple in nature.
16. Dr. Ramachandra., Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, is examined as Pw2 and through him OPD slip, x-ray film and Inpatient case sheet are got marked as Ex.P12 and Ex.P14.
P.W.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 28-08-2025 for disability assessment.
PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent residual physical disability of both right upper limb at 42.4% and to the whole body at 14%.

Beeregowda C K vs Kumar on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182576943/
4 17.
If the cross examination of PW.2 is carefully perused, PW.2 has not given treatment to the petitioner.

It is admitted by PW.2 that it is quite natural that the restriction of movement in upper limb will be there in aged persons and that if there is restriction of movement and stiffness in the body, physiotherapy treatment will be suggested and that in the discharge summary there is no advise given to the petitioner to take physiotherapy treatment.

As per the evidence of PW.2, the fracture is united and there is improvement in the health condition of the petitioner from the date of discharge till the date on which he was examined to assess the disability.
It is further admitted by PW.2 that they will not suggest to remove the implant to an aged person.

Hence, considering the evidence of the PW.2 it can be said that since petitioner is person aged about 74 years it is quite natural that some amount of pain and restriction of movement will be there due to the age factor.

Hence, this court inclines to consider the disability at 10% instead of 14%.
18.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
19. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury and two simple injuries.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
20. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced medical bill for Rs.2,03,647/-, as per Ex.P10.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.2,03,647/-
21.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 74 years and he was agriculturalist and was earning sum of Rs.6,00,000/- per annum.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and the place of residence of the petitioner takes the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
22.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and two simple injuries and has taken treatment for 8 days as inpatient in Grass Life Health care, Channarayapatna.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 4 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for 4 months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.66,000/- (16,500X4) towards loss of income during the laid down period .
23. From the evidence of Pw.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at True life Grasslife Health care, Channarayapatna.
Further for 8 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/-
taking into consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.

Beeregowda C K vs Kumar on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182576943/
5 24.
The petitioner has contended that, he was aged about 74 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P9/Aadhar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 25-06-1948 that means he was aged about 76 years.
Hence considering the copy of Aadhaar card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 76 years at the time of accident.

25. So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.16,500/- p.m and if 10% of loss of earning capacity is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 76 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of above 65 years.
So by applying the multiplier '05' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.99,000/- (i.e., 16,500 x 10% x 5 x12 )-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.99,000/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
26. The petitioner at his age of 76 years has suffered grievous injury which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of comfort and amenities

, thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-

2. Medical expenses Rs. 2,03,647/-
 3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 66,000/-
 laid up period  4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant

Rs . 25,000/-
 charges and nourishing food

5. Future Loss of Income Rs. 99,000/-
 6. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs. 30,000/-

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,93,647/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Ninety Three Thousand Six Hundred Forty Seven only).
27.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with 2 nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the rider of the offending vehicle had driving license to ride the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question were valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2, this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly, Issue No. 2 is answered.
28. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

Beeregowda C K vs Kumar on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182576943/
6

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.4,93,647/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Ninety Three Thousand Six Hundred Forty Seven only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 7th day of November 2025.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl. SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
